verdict.summary: Build a public GitHub App and have each customer install it on selected repositories; this is self-serve and does not require a general production review. Use GitHub App installation tokens for tenant background automation, adding GitHub App user access only when an action must be attributable to a particular connected user. Marketplace listing is optional and introduces a separate review process; paid Marketplace distribution also has publisher-verification, financial-onboarding, and installation requirements.
verdict.activeEffort: 1–3 days, plus configuration and testing, mostly implementing secure token handling, webhook processing, and least-privilege permission design.
verdict.mainGate: A customer must be an organization owner or repository administrator to install the App; sensitive organization-level, repository-administration, and repository-creation permissions require organization-owner approval.

recommendation.text: Register an organization-owned public GitHub App, distribute its installation URL directly to each tenant, and request only repository permissions required by enabled agent features. Use installation access tokens for autonomous background work and GitHub App user access tokens only for explicitly user-authorized, user-attributed actions; do not use a broad legacy OAuth App unless its breadth is genuinely required.

sources.quote: In general, GitHub Apps are preferred over OAuth apps. GitHub Apps use fine-grained permissions, give the user more control over which repositories the app can access, and use short-lived tokens.
You can share the app with other developers via GitHub Marketplace or by making the app public.

essentials.text: Use installation access tokens for background work; they expire after 1 hour. GitHub App user access tokens expire after 8 hours by default; request offline_access to receive a refresh token, which is valid for 6 months. Refresh through POST https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token with grant_type=refresh_token and atomically replace both stored tokens because refresh-token rotation invalidates the old refresh token and old access token.

sources.quote: Installation access tokens expire after a predefined amount of time (currently 1 hour).
To receive an expiring user access token and a refresh token for this authorization, set this value to offline_access . No other scopes are supported for GitHub Apps.
Once you use a refresh token, that refresh token and the old user access token will no longer work.

essentials.text: For the GitHub App user authorization flow, send users to https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize, register exact production callback URL(s), validate an unguessable state value, and use authorization-code PKCE with S256. Do not rely on wildcard redirects unless all matching routes are controlled.

sources.quote: Direct the user to this URL, and add any necessary query parameters from the following list of parameters: https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize
When wildcard matching is disabled, the redirect URL must exactly match the callback URL.
Only the S256 code challenge method is accepted.

essentials.text: GitHub does not document a Google-style App development mode or test-user cap. A user or organization can register up to 100 GitHub Apps, while installations per account are not limited; for Marketplace billing tests, use a separate development App with the production configuration and a draft listing.

sources.quote: A user or organization can register up to 100 GitHub Apps, but there is no limit to how many GitHub Apps can be installed on an account.

essentials.text: A GitHub App user token receives 5,000 requests/hour, or 15,000 requests/hour for a user in a GitHub Enterprise Cloud organization. Non-Enterprise installation tokens start at 5,000 requests/hour and scale by repositories and users, capped at 12,500 requests/hour; Enterprise Cloud installations receive 15,000 requests/hour.

sources.quote: The rate limit for a user access token is 5,000 requests per hour. If the user is a member of a GitHub Enterprise Cloud organization, the rate limit is 15,000 requests per hour.
The rate limit is capped at 12,500 requests per hour.

steps.title: Register an organization-owned public GitHub App

detail.text: In the owning organization's Settings, open Developer settings → GitHub Apps → New GitHub App. Register the production App under the company organization, select Public, and enter the product name, homepage, callback URL, and webhook URL so unaffiliated customer accounts can install it.

sources.quote: You can register a GitHub App under your personal account or under any organization you own.

detail.text: Use this draft in the App permission design and customer-facing installation explanation, retaining only permissions mapped to enabled product features.

steps.output:
Permissions rationale:
• Metadata read: identify installed repositories.
• Contents read/write: inspect and create approved file changes.
• Issues read/write: read context and create or update approved issues.
• Pull requests read/write: inspect PR context and create or update approved PRs.
Do not request organization administration, repository administration, repository creation, Actions, checks, deployments, discussions, or member access unless a named feature requires it.

steps.title: Configure permissions, webhooks, and secure credentials

detail.text: In the GitHub App settings, set only the approved repository permissions, subscribe only to webhooks your service processes, generate and securely store the App private key, and configure webhook-signature validation. Keep sensitive organization, repository-administration, and repository-creation permissions disabled unless a defined feature needs them.

steps.title: Implement installation and optional user authorization flows

detail.text: Implement JWT-based installation-token creation for background work, refresh installation tokens before their one-hour expiry, and isolate tokens by installation ID. If actions need a connected person's authority, implement the GitHub App user flow with state, S256 PKCE, offline_access, encrypted token storage, and refresh-token rotation handling.
